answer: Trust-graph min-cut screening treats accounts as a meadow of nodes joined by mutual endorsements. Honest users form dense, well-mixed links; a sybil cluster connects to them only through a few attack edges, like a karst sinkhole draining through narrow cracks. Each fake head needs its own real endorsement to stay inside the cut, so cost rises with every one. Writing a sonnet of fake praise among themselves earns nothing.
